title: Vendor-neutral and Production-grade Job Power Management in High Performance Computing
problem: Existing power management solutions lack portability due to vendor-specific implementations, do not support non-MPI applications, and provide limited user-level customization. Production HPC systems require reliable telemetry and control mechanisms for dynamic power management across distributed systems.
motivation: Power management and energy efficiency are critical for exascale computing and beyond.
method: The framework leverages Flux as a foundation for vendor-neutral job scheduling and power management. flux-power-monitor provides telemetry collection across heterogeneous systems with 0.4% overhead. flux-power-manager implements a proportional sharing policy and a hierarchical FFT-based dynamic power management algorithm (FPP) that dynamically adjusts power budgets based on workload characteristics.
key_novelty: A hierarchical FFT-based dynamic power management algorithm (FPP) that enables vendor-neutral, production-grade power capping with user-level customization for non-MPI workloads.
contributions: Vendor-neutral power telemetry framework (flux-power-monitor) with 0.4% monitoring overhead
Hierarchical FFT-based dynamic power management algorithm (FPP) achieving 1-20% energy improvements
Production-validated deployment on Lassen (IBM Power AC922) and Tioga (HPE Cray EX235A) systems
Support for non-MPI applications with user-level power customization

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 1% vs proportional sharing, 20% vs IBM static power capping

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: vendor-neutral dynamic power management for HPC systems
